seoTitle: Connect Facebook Pages to GoHighLevel: Setup Guide
metaDescription: Link your Facebook Page to GoHighLevel to manage Messenger conversations, sync leads, and automate follow-ups from your CRM.
intro: If you're running conversations and leads through a Facebook Page, GoHighLevel can pull all of that into the same dashboard where you already manage email, SMS, and workflows. Instead of logging into Meta Business Suite separately, you connect the page once and let GoHighLevel handle the syncing. This guide walks through where that connection actually lives inside the platform, what the account-linking screen looks like, and what to check once a page is attached so messages and leads actually flow through.

steps.heading: Start from your GoHighLevel dashboard
steps.body: Log into your sub-account and look at the Launchpad, which GoHighLevel shows new and returning users as a personalized setup checklist — items like adding contacts, setting up communication channels, and launching campaigns, each with a progress percentage. Facebook isn't listed here directly, but this is a useful home base because it confirms which foundational pieces (payments, phone numbers, email sending) are already switched on before you start layering a social integration on top. If your account is brand new, expect most of these items to sit at 0%, which is normal.

image.caption: The GoHighLevel Launchpad, showing the account's foundational setup progress before any Facebook connection is made.

steps.heading: Open Marketing and find the Social Planner
steps.body: From the left-hand menu, click Marketing, then the Social Planner tab. This is where GoHighLevel manages every social account tied to the sub-account, and it's the actual home for linking a Facebook Page — not a hidden settings menu, just a normal tab under Marketing. If you've never connected anything here, the page opens with an empty state prompting you to pick a network.

steps.heading: Connect your Facebook Page
steps.body: The Social Planner screen lays out a row of account cards — Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, YouTube, plus a second row for Pinterest, Threads, Bluesky, Google Business Profile, and Community. Click Connect on the Facebook card and you're handed off to Meta's own login and page-selection flow. Pick the Facebook account tied to your business, then choose the specific Page you want linked — GoHighLevel only manages Pages you explicitly select here, not your whole personal profile.

image.caption: The Social Planner's account-connection screen, where Facebook sits alongside Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, and YouTube as a one-click Connect card.

steps.heading: Grant the permissions Meta asks for
steps.body: Once you're inside Meta's authorization flow, you'll be asked to approve specific permissions — access to manage the Page, read and respond to messages, and view Page content. Approve all of them; if you decline any single permission, GoHighLevel typically can't sync that Page's conversations or leads reliably. This step happens on Meta's domain, not GoHighLevel's, so don't be surprised by the visual switch — it's expected, and it's the same authorization screen any third-party Facebook integration uses.

steps.heading: Confirm the Page shows as connected
steps.body: After authorization finishes, you're returned to the Social Planner, and the Facebook card should now show your Page name instead of a Connect button. This is the moment to double check you linked the right Page, especially if your business manages more than one — GoHighLevel doesn't stop you from connecting the wrong one, and unwinding it later means disconnecting and reauthorizing from scratch.

steps.heading: Check that Messenger conversations land in Conversations
steps.body: With the Page connected, incoming Messenger messages should start appearing in GoHighLevel's Conversations tab alongside your SMS and email threads, and new message senders should generate contact records automatically. Send yourself a test message from the connected Page to confirm it shows up before you rely on it for real customer traffic — a missed permission during authorization is the most common reason messages don't sync.

steps.heading: Build a workflow around new Facebook leads
steps.body: Once messages are flowing in, the real payoff is automation. In the Workflows section, you can trigger a sequence whenever a new contact arrives from Facebook — an instant auto-reply, a tag that routes them to the right team, or a follow-up sequence a few hours later if no one's responded. Keep the first automated message short and conversational; a canned corporate reply is the fastest way to make someone stop replying to a Page they just messaged.

faq.question: Do I need a Meta account to connect my Facebook Page?
faq.answer: Yes. You authorize the connection through your own Meta login during setup, and you need admin access to the Facebook Page itself for GoHighLevel to be allowed to manage it.

faq.question: Can I manage Facebook Messenger from GoHighLevel?
faq.answer: Yes. Once a Page is connected and permissions are approved, Messenger conversations appear in GoHighLevel's Conversations tab alongside your other channels.

faq.question: Can I automate responses to new Facebook leads?
faq.answer: Yes. Workflows can trigger off a new Facebook contact or message, sending an automatic reply, applying tags, or starting a follow-up sequence.

faq.question: What permissions does this integration require?
faq.answer: Meta will ask you to approve Page management and messaging permissions during the connection flow. Declining any of them can break message or lead syncing.

faq.question: Where in GoHighLevel do I actually connect Facebook?
faq.answer: Under Marketing → Social Planner. It's the same screen used to connect Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok, and other networks, not a separate Facebook-only settings page.
